_____________________________________________________  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DEEPAK MAHESHWARI  Order 28/04/2017  Heard learned counsel for the petitioner.
This criminal revision petition has been preferred on behalf of accused-petition challenging the order dated 19.04.2017 whereby application filed under Section 70(2) Cr.P.C. was rejected.

On perusal of the documents annexed, it appears that the complaint came to be filed against accused-petitioner for the offence under Section 7(I)(iii) and 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, on which cognizance was taken against him vide order dated 7 rd August, 2007.
The accused was summoned through bailable warrant.

It appears that he remained absent on 5th May,
2014 and was called through arrest warrant.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the accused (2 of 2) [CRLMP-2172/2017] has been facing trial since 2007 and because of serious ailment of his brother-in-law who was suffering from cancer kept him busy in regard to his treatment and could not remain present before the Court.
Thereafter, he was called through arrest warrant.
It is further stated that the report with regard to sample of 'Arhar Dal' has not yet been received from Central Food Laboratory.
So no effective proceedings have been conducted against the accused- petitioner and the same has not been hampered because of the absence of the accused-petitioner.
The facts stated by learned counsel for the petitioner are substantiated on perusal of the documents annexed with the petition.
In view of above, it appears that calling the accused- petitioner by way of arrest warrant will merely be an abuse of process of law.
Accordingly, this petition is allowed and the order impugned dated 19.04.2017 is quashed and set aside.

Learned trial Court will issue order to Mohanswaroop Khandelwal vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr on 28 April, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54935942/
1 summon the accused-petitioner through bailable warrant.
